concepts.title: EMI Amortization of Loans
concepts.definition: An equated monthly instalment (EMI) repays both interest and principal in equal periodic payments over the loan term. For principal P at periodic rate r over n periods, EMI = P r (1+r)^n / ((1+r)^n - 1); each payment first covers that period's interest, the remainder reduces the principal, which is amortization.
concepts.key_idea: Early EMIs are mostly interest because interest is charged on the outstanding principal; as the principal falls, the interest slice shrinks and the principal slice grows.
question_patterns: Find the EMI for a loan of {p} at {r} per period for {n} periods.
A loan of {p} is repaid in {n} equal instalments at rate {r}; compute the instalment.
In amortization, why does the interest part of an EMI fall over time?
Compute the total interest paid over the loan if the EMI is {emi} for {n} payments.
What does amortization schedule of a loan show?

concepts.title: Compound Annual Growth Rate
concepts.definition: The compound annual growth rate (CAGR) is the constant yearly rate at which an initial value V0 must grow to reach a final value V1 after n years: CAGR = (V1/V0)^(1/n) - 1. It smooths uneven year-to-year growth into one equivalent rate.
concepts.key_idea: CAGR ignores the path and keeps only the endpoints: a value that doubled in 8 years has CAGR 2^(1/8) - 1, about 9 percent per year, whatever the swings in between.
question_patterns: A company's revenue grew from {v0} to {v1} in {n} years; find the CAGR.
Find the compound annual growth rate between the two given values.
If sales grow at CAGR {g} percent, what will the value be after {n} years?
Why is CAGR better than the average of yearly growth rates?
An investment of {v0} became {v1} in {n} years; express the growth as one annual rate.

concepts.title: Depreciation Written Down Value
concepts.definition: Depreciation is the fall in an asset's value with use and age. Under the written down value method the asset loses a fixed percentage d of its current value each year, so value after n years = cost times (1 - d/100)^n, a compound decay.
concepts.key_idea: The percentage applies to the reducing balance, not the original cost, so early years show larger absolute depreciation. Scrap value is what remains after n years.
question_patterns: A machine costing {cost} depreciates at {d} percent per year; find its value after {n} years.
Find the scrap value of an asset after {n} years at {d} percent written down depreciation.
By what factor does an asset's value multiply over {n} years at {d} percent per year?
Compare straight-line and written down value depreciation.
A vehicle bought for {cost} loses {d} percent yearly; when is it worth half?

concepts.title: Annuity Present and Future Value
concepts.definition: An annuity is a sequence of equal periodic payments A. The future value after n periods at rate r is FV = A ((1+r)^n - 1) / r, the accumulated amount of every payment with interest. The present value is PV = A (1 - (1+r)^(-n)) / r, the lump sum today that finances the whole stream.
concepts.key_idea: Future value asks what the stream grows into; present value asks what it is worth today. A loan valuation is the present value of its repayment stream, which is why PV of the EMIs equals the principal.
question_patterns: Find the future value of an annuity of {a} per period for {n} periods at {r} per period.
What lump sum today equals an annuity of {a} for {n} periods at {r}?
Compute the present value of the annuity and verify it funds all payments.
A sinking fund receives {a} per period at {r}; find the corpus after {n} periods.
Distinguish present value from future value of an annuity.

concepts.title: Perpetuity and Perpetual Payments
concepts.definition: A perpetuity is an annuity that pays forever. Because n grows without bound, its present value collapses to PV = A / r: the lump sum whose periodic interest exactly funds the payment A forever, leaving the principal intact.
concepts.key_idea: No growth term survives in a perpetuity: an infinite stream has a finite value because distant payments are discounted to almost nothing. Endowed scholarships and consul bonds are classic perpetuities.
question_patterns: Find the present value of a perpetuity paying {a} per period at rate {r}.
How much money must be endowed to fund {a} forever at {r} percent?
What is a perpetuity and why does it have a finite value?
At what rate does a payment of {a} forever cost {pv} today?
Compare the present value of a 100-year annuity with a perpetuity at the same rate.

worked_examples.q: A loan of 500000 at 0.8 percent per month is repaid over 60 months. Find the EMI and total interest.
worked_examples.a: r = 0.008, n = 60. (1.008)^60 is about 1.6130. EMI = 500000 x 0.008 x 1.6130 / 0.6130, which is about 10525. Total paid = 10525 x 60 = 631500, so total interest is about 131500.

worked_examples.q: A machine bought for 800000 depreciates at 10 percent per year under the written down value method. Find its book value after 3 years.
